text.p: Schedule of matches in the French first division this weekend (standings in parentheses, all kick-off times GMT):
Thursday:
Rennes (13) v Monaco (1) 1930

Monaco goalkeeper Fabien Barthez sidelined following surgery on Monday on broken bone in right cheek. He had played the previous day in 0-0 home draw with Auxerre wearing a protective bandage. Leaders will be looking for win ahead of Newcastle's UEFA Cup visit on Tuesday against side who have lost only once at home this season.
Friday:
Bastia (3) v Montpellier (12) 1900

Corsicans will be looking to bounce back from worst defeat of season, 3-0 at Nantes last weekend. Montpellier are on song and unbeaten this year in league, climbing out of relegation zone to relative mid-table security.
Nice (20) v Nantes (6) 1900
Nantes, unbeaten in 21 league games, are gunning for berth in Europe and, with four away wins in succession, should be too strong for basement side Nice.
Auxerre (7) v Cannes (14) 1900

Champions looking for first win in seven matches and first goal in France in six -- although they scored in 3-1 European Cup loss away to Borussia Dortmund last week -- as they look to hang on to place in Europe. Cannes have easily worst attack over longer term with only 16 goals in 28 league games.
Lille (17) v Nancy (19) 1900

City of Lille could be facing double burst bubble this year with relegation from football's top flight after disappointment of failed bid to stage 2004 Olympic Games. Nancy look even more likely for the drop.
Le Havre (15) v Paris St Germain (2) 1900

PSG will be looking to renew challenge to leaders Monaco after recovering their self-esteem with first home win in four months against Lyon on Sunday. They are also near full strength again with defenders Jimmy Algerino and Didier Domi back in training.
Marseille (9) v Strasbourg (4) 1900
Former European champions are going through lean spell, conceding seven goals in last two games, and will find confident Strasbourg side featuring league's top scorer David Zitelli tough to beat.
Saturday:
Metz (8) v Lens (16) 1700
Lens play under new coach Roger Lemerre after sacking of Slavo Muslin. Metz, gunning for place in Europe, beat leaders Monaco in their last home game.
Bordeaux (5) v Caen (18) 1900

Unbeaten in the league this year, Bordeaux should put another nail in Caen's relegation coffin. France's Ibrahim Ba is back in training after recovering from injury, while fellow midfielder Stephane Ziani will have to wear a brace on his fractured hand.
Lyon (11) v Guingamp (10) 1900

Guingamp's counter-attacking game in which Stephane Carnot plays pivotal role has helped them take four points from last two games against big guns PSG and Marseille. Lyon will be looking to bounce back from 3-1 loss at PSG.
